newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Asian dollar deposits quietly steady in dull trade.
newsitem.headline: Asian dollar deposits quietly steady in dull trade.

text.p: Asian dollar deposit rates were quietly steady in dull trade this afternoon due to a lack of fresh incentives, dealers said on Thursday.
"The market became quiet this afternoon. There was some short-term buying this morning," a local dealer said.
"Most people have taken their positions and are waiting for new directions from the figures of the U.S. December producer price index and the U.S. jobless claims," he said.
Figures for the U.S. December producer price index and the U.S. jobless claims are due to be released later on Thursday.
In short dates, Thursday/Friday and week-fixed rose 1/16 percentage point to a common 5-3/8 5-1/4 percent from Wednesday's common 5-5/16 5-3/16 percent.

Among term rates, one-month remained unchanged at Wednesday's 5-1/2 5-3/8 percent, two-months eased 1/16 percentage point to 5-1/2 5-3/8 percent from Wednesday's 5-9/17 5-7/16 percent. Four-months, five-months remained at Wednesday's common 5-9/16 5-7/16 percent.
Nine-months remained at Wednesday's 5-3/4 5-5/8 percent and twelve-months unchanged at Wednesday's 5-7/8 5-3/4 percent.
